title: Fleet parity sample for the public R1: OSWorld LibreOffice tasks scored by upstream DesktopEnv.evaluate() on the Myco fleet and on OSWorld's reference environment
ruling: Lead rulings 2026-11-27 14:05Z (#741 comment 7220313158: parity acceptance required; same scripted known-good and known-bad sequences on both, graded by the upstream evaluator; any mismatch is a stated gap), 14:37Z (#741 comment 7220987945: keep the parity harness and the exact host requirement; do not run it), 15:21Z (#741 comment 7221935698: UTM approved as the reference hypervisor, a stated deviation).
actionFormat: Each action is what AnthropicAgent hands DesktopEnv.step: {action_type: tool_use, command: <pyautogui code>} runs through PythonController.execute_python_command (the controller prefixes `import pyautogui; import time`); DONE and FAIL are upstream's own special actions. No model is involved.
selectionRule: Pre-declared before any parity run. Tasks whose known-good sequence does not depend on the seed file's contents (so it can be written without downloading OSWorld's assets), covering all three LibreOffice domains and the getters these domains use: vm_file on .xlsx and .docx, the accessibility tree, and the infeasible rule. Gap in coverage, stated: no task here grades a .pptx through vm_file (33 of the 47 impress tasks do).

fleet.description: The Myco Linux fleet desktop (src/benchmark/upstream/fleet/Dockerfile) via the myco-fleet DesktopEnv provider.

reference.description: OSWorld's own guest image Ubuntu-arm.zip (huggingface.co/datasets/xlangai/ubuntu_osworld), its in-guest controller and OSWorld's evaluator unchanged, booted in UTM (QEMU with HVF) via the utm-reference provider. STATED DEVIATION from OSWorld's VMware reference: only the hypervisor differs.

rule: Parity must pass before any live run. For each task: the reference must score the known-good sequence as a pass (exactly 1.0) and the known-bad sequence as a fail (a gradable score below 1.0); otherwise the task is SEQUENCE_INVALID. The fleet matches when it also scores known-good as a pass and known-bad as a fail; anything else, an ungradable fleet run included, is a GAP. Parity passes only when every task matches; a mismatch is a stated gap, and a SEQUENCE_INVALID task blocks parity until the sample is amended (a new sample version, decided before any further run).
